description: We are a two-member student research and development team from India combining backgrounds in Artificial Intelligence, Data Science (IIT Madras certified), and software design. Our goal is to build an end-to-end data-driven prototype using NASA open datasets to solve real-world space exploration challenges. Team roster is currently finalized.
summary: AstroBuddy is a calm health-monitoring software prototype for astronauts on long missions. A wearable band and radiation badge would send readings automatically, so astronauts do not need to type anything. AstroBuddy brings blood pressure, heart rate, oxygen, glucose, sleep, stress, exercise and radiation into one dashboard. It stays quiet when readings are steady. When a reading moves outside an illustrative range, it explains the concern in plain language, suggests calm next steps, and shows how urgent cases could be flagged for medical review. It also includes an optional, private cycle-tracker demo for crew members who menstruate. The prototype uses simulated data and fictional crew. AstroBuddy matters because astronauts far from Earth carry much of the responsibility for spotting health changes themselves, and clear, calm guidance may help them act early without added stress.
details:
What it does: AstroBuddy is a decision-support dashboard concept for astronauts. It shows a status ring, a plain-language message, suggested next steps, trend lines, an event log, a calm-breathing guide, and demo-only alert buttons.

How it works: A simulated wearable stream updates readings every 1.5 seconds. Each reading is compared with illustrative ranges (steady, watch, review needed). When something changes, the dashboard explains it calmly and suggests steps. It builds on sensing that already exists, such as the CSA Bio-Monitor smart shirt.

Benefits and intended impact: Astronauts have little time and no hospital nearby, so automatic sensing and calm guidance could reduce workload and stress. These are intended benefits, not clinically tested results.

Tools: HTML, CSS, JavaScript, GitHub Pages, Canva (slides), Nunito font.

What is creative: calm by design, quiet when steady, a built-in breathing guide, and an optional cycle tracker for inclusive health tracking.

What we considered: crews cannot type in data, so readings arrive automatically. Guidance follows onboard procedures and does not give medicine doses. All data is simulated, ranges are illustrative, and a real system would need validated thresholds and clinical review. We used design thinking (Empathize, Define, Ideate, Prototype, Test with five simulated scenarios).

AI use: Claude, an AI assistant by Anthropic, helped with parts of the code and wording. The Solution_concept, direction and design decisions are ours.
